```{r config}
tx <- list(
  # the paragraphs, as already parsed from the speeches: one row per paragraph
  input_file = "unga_paragraphs.csv",  # in unga/inputs/
  cols = c(id = "id", year = "Year", para = "para_uid", text = "raw_text"),
  # a paragraph is analyzed only if it reads as one
  min_words = 20L,  # shorter paragraphs are headers or fragments
  procedural = c(  # the presiding officer's words, not the speaker's
    "will now hear an address", "request protocol to escort",
    "escorted (from|to) the rostrum", "i now (give|call on|invite)",
    "on behalf of the (general )?assembly,? i (wish|would like) to thank"),
  drop_words = c("united", "nations", "general", "assembly", "session",
                 "president", "mr", "madam", "secretary", "delegation",
                 "excellency", "distinguished", "delegates"),  # in every speech
  seed = 2026L,
  min_docfreq = 20L,  # drop words in fewer paragraphs than this
  run_searchK = FALSE,  # TRUE to compare numbers of topics (hours at this size)
  K_grid = c(5L, seq(10L, 100L, 10L)),  # then a finer grid around the best
  K = 40L,  # set from the searchK plots
  spline_df = 5L,  # flexibility of the year trend
  n_words = 20L,  # words per topic shown to the codebook model
  n_examples = 5L,  # example paragraphs per topic shown to the codebook model
  n_draws = 25L,  # draws of topic shares behind each trend interval
  workers = 4L,  # each holds a copy of the data; 4 fits in 32 GB
  use_openrouter = TRUE,  # FALSE at work
  steps = tibble::tribble(
    ~step, ~base_url_env, ~api_key_env, ~model,
    "codebook", "COMPASS_LARGE_URL", "COMPASS_LARGE_KEY", "LARGE-MODEL"))

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(here); library(stm); library(splines); library(viridis)
  library(tidyverse)  # tidyverse last so its verbs win
})
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
set.seed(tx$seed)
options(hot_topic.project = "unga")  # paths: unga/inputs, unga/outputs
source(here::here("topics", "topics_source.R"))  # the topics project's functions
if (isTRUE(tx$use_openrouter)) {
  source(here::here("topics", "llm_openrouter.R"))
  tx$steps$model <- open_router_models[tx$steps$step]
}
dir.create(p_out(), showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# The speeches

```{r input}
#| results: asis
raw_in <- p_in(tx$input_file)
raw <- readr::read_csv(raw_in, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = readr::cols(
  .default = readr::col_character()))
miss <- setdiff(unname(tx$cols), names(raw))
if (length(miss)) stop(tx$input_file, " is missing: ", str_c(miss, collapse = ", "))
# Internally para_uid is the paragraph's key (speech-position), which is what
# the shared functions expect; outputs give back your id and position.
all_paras <- raw |>
  dplyr::transmute(id = .data[[tx$cols[["id"]]]],
                   Year = as.integer(.data[[tx$cols[["year"]]]]),
                   para_id = as.integer(.data[[tx$cols[["para"]]]]),
                   # a working copy with spaces collapsed, for screening and
                   # tokens only; it is never written out, so your raw_text
                   # stays exactly as parsed
                   text = str_squish(.data[[tx$cols[["text"]]]])) |>
  dplyr::mutate(para_uid = str_c(id, "-", para_id))
stopifnot("Year must be a whole number on every row" = !anyNA(all_paras$Year),
          "para_uid must be the paragraph's position, a whole number" = !anyNA(all_paras$para_id),
          "id + para_uid must be unique" = !anyDuplicated(all_paras$para_uid),
          "a speech id must have one year" =
            nrow(dplyr::distinct(all_paras, id, Year)) == dplyr::n_distinct(all_paras$id))
writeLines(glue::glue("{format(nrow(all_paras), big.mark = ',')} paragraphs from \\
  {format(dplyr::n_distinct(all_paras$id), big.mark = ',')} speeches, \\
  {min(all_paras$Year)} to {max(all_paras$Year)}."))
```

```{r speeches-per-year}
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: "Speeches in the corpus each year."
all_paras |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, Year) |>
  dplyr::count(Year) |>
  ggplot(aes(Year, n)) +
  geom_col(fill = viridis(1, begin = 0.35)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "speeches")
```

# Which paragraphs are analyzed

The paragraphs are used exactly as they were parsed from the speeches, so they line up with every other analysis of the same paragraphs. None is merged, split, or edited. A paragraph is left out, whole, if it

1. **has no complete sentence**: no sentence ending in a period, question mark, or exclamation mark. These are headers, labels, dates, and lines such as "Meeting/Event" or "[Auto-generated transcript]";
2. **is the presiding officer speaking**: introducing the speaker or thanking them, matched by the phrases in `tx$procedural`;
3. **is shorter than `r tx$min_words` words**: salutations and fragments that carry no subject.

```{r screen}
#| results: asis
procedural_rx <- str_c(tx$procedural, collapse = "|")
screened <- all_paras |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_words = str_count(text, "\\S+"),
    reason = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(text) | text == "" ~ "empty",
      !str_detect(text, "[.!?][\"')\\]]*(\\s|$)") ~ "no complete sentence",
      str_detect(str_to_lower(text), procedural_rx) ~ "presiding officer",
      n_words < tx$min_words ~ str_c("under ", tx$min_words, " words"),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_))
paragraphs <- dplyr::filter(screened, is.na(reason))
dropped <- dplyr::filter(screened, !is.na(reason))
arrow::write_parquet(dplyr::select(dropped, id, para_uid = para_id, Year, reason),
                     p_out("dropped_paragraphs.parquet"))

dplyr::count(screened, reason = dplyr::coalesce(reason, "analyzed"), name = "paragraphs") |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = paragraphs / sum(paragraphs)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(paragraphs)) |>
  tbl_paged(caption = "Paragraphs analyzed and left out, by reason.")
```

```{r dropped-by-year}
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: "Share of paragraphs left out each year. A year that loses far more than the others rests on a different mix of text."
screened |>
  dplyr::group_by(Year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dropped = mean(!is.na(reason))) |>
  ggplot(aes(Year, dropped)) +
  geom_col(fill = viridis(1, begin = 0.6)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "left out")
```

```{r dropped-examples}
#| results: asis
withr::with_seed(tx$seed, dropped |>
  dplyr::group_by(reason) |>
  dplyr::slice_sample(n = 2) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()) |>
  dplyr::mutate(title = str_c(reason, " | ", id, " paragraph ", para_id),
                text = str_trunc(text, 300)) |>
  tbl_records("title", "text", caption = "Two paragraphs left out for each reason. If a real paragraph appears here, loosen the rule that caught it.")
```

# Document-term matrix

Words are lowercased and kept only if purely alphabetic. Stopwords, month and weekday names, and words every speech uses (`r str_c(tx$drop_words, collapse = ", ")`) are removed. Words in fewer than `r tx$min_docfreq` paragraphs are dropped.

```{r dtm}
#| results: asis
tokens <- clean_tokens(paragraphs, tx$drop_words)
stm_in <- stm_input(tokens, tx$min_docfreq)
# stm needs a plain data frame in the same row order as the documents, with
# the year spline as ordinary columns yr1, yr2, ...
meta <- tibble(para_uid = names(stm_in$documents)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(paragraphs, by = "para_uid") |>
  as.data.frame()
bs <- splines::ns(meta$Year, df = tx$spline_df)
colnames(bs) <- str_c("yr", seq_len(ncol(bs)))
meta <- cbind(meta, as.data.frame(bs))
prev_form <- as.formula(str_c("~ ", str_c(colnames(bs), collapse = " + ")))
writeLines(glue::glue("{format(length(stm_in$documents), big.mark = ',')} paragraphs and \\
  {format(length(stm_in$vocab), big.mark = ',')} words enter the model; \\
  {nrow(paragraphs) - length(stm_in$documents)} paragraphs had no word left."))
```

# How many topics

Each candidate number of topics is fitted on most of the text and scored on the rest. Take the smallest number where held-out likelihood has flattened and residual dispersion has stopped falling, then break ties on coherence and exclusivity. The first pass is broad; narrow `K_grid` around the best values and run again. Each grid is saved under its own name, so the passes do not overwrite each other.

```{r searchK}
if (isTRUE(tx$run_searchK)) {
  grid_file <- p_out(str_c("searchK_", min(tx$K_grid), "-", max(tx$K_grid), "_",
                           length(tx$K_grid), ".parquet"))
  future::plan(future::multisession, workers = tx$workers)
  ho <- stm::make.heldout(stm_in$documents, stm_in$vocab, seed = tx$seed)
  metrics <- cached(grid_file, raw_in,
    furrr::future_map(tx$K_grid, function(k) {
      fit <- stm::stm(ho$documents, ho$vocab, K = k, init.type = "Spectral",
                      prevalence = prev_form, data = meta, verbose = FALSE)
      tibble(K = k,
             heldout = stm::eval.heldout(fit, ho$missing)$expected.heldout,
             dispersion = stm::checkResiduals(fit, ho$documents)$dispersion,
             coherence = mean(stm::semanticCoherence(fit, ho$documents)),
             exclusivity = mean(stm::exclusivity(fit)))
    }, .options = furrr::furrr_options(seed = tx$seed)) |> purrr::list_rbind())
  future::plan(future::sequential)
  metrics |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-K) |>
    ggplot(aes(K, value)) +
    geom_line(color = viridis(1, begin = 0.35)) + geom_point() +
    facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_y") + labs(y = NULL)
} else glue::glue("Search skipped; K = {tx$K}.")
```

# The topics

Year enters topic prevalence as a spline, so each topic's share can rise and fall over the period. Spectral initialization makes the fit reproducible. The fit is saved as `stm_fit.rds` and reloaded on later renders; delete it to refit.

```{r stm-fit}
stm_fit <- cached(p_out("stm_fit.rds"), raw_in,
  stm::stm(stm_in$documents, stm_in$vocab, K = tx$K, init.type = "Spectral",
           prevalence = prev_form, data = meta, verbose = FALSE))
K <- ncol(stm_fit$theta)
if (K != tx$K) stop("stm_fit.rds has K = ", K, " but tx$K = ", tx$K,
                    ". Delete stm_fit.rds, then re-render.")
theta <- stm_fit$theta
colnames(theta) <- str_c("topic_", seq_len(K))
```

Each paragraph is assigned its most likely topic. **Entropy R²** (0 to 1) says how sharply paragraphs sort into topics overall; **AvePP** is the average topic share among a topic's own paragraphs, with about 0.7 the usual floor.

```{r modal}
#| results: asis
paragraph_theta <- meta |>
  dplyr::select(para_uid, id, para_id, Year) |>
  dplyr::bind_cols(tibble::as_tibble(theta)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(topic = max.col(theta, ties.method = "first"),
                theta_max = theta[cbind(dplyr::row_number(), topic)])
entropy_r2 <- 1 - (-sum(theta * log(theta + 1e-12))) / (nrow(theta) * log(K))

words <- stm::labelTopics(stm_fit, n = tx$n_words)
topic_summary <- tibble(
  topic = seq_len(K),
  prevalence = colMeans(theta),
  frex = apply(words$frex, 1, str_c, collapse = ", "),
  prob = apply(words$prob, 1, str_c, collapse = ", ")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(paragraph_theta |>
                     dplyr::group_by(topic) |>
                     dplyr::summarise(n_paras = dplyr::n(), avepp = mean(theta_max)),
                   by = "topic")

# Outputs carry no text: they join back to the paragraphs on id + para_uid.
# Shares are rounded to 4 decimals, which keeps the file small.
theta_out <- p_out("paragraph_topics.parquet")
paragraph_theta |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, para_uid = para_id, Year, topic, theta_max = round(theta_max, 4),
                   dplyr::across(dplyr::starts_with("topic_"), function(x) round(x, 4))) |>
  arrow::write_parquet(theta_out)
arrow::write_parquet(topic_summary, p_out("topic_summary.parquet"))

writeLines(glue::glue("Entropy R2 = {round(entropy_r2, 3)}. \\
  Topics with AvePP under 0.7: {sum(topic_summary$avepp < 0.7, na.rm = TRUE)} of {K}."))
```

## Topic labels

One call per topic, all in parallel, with the larger model. Each call sees only that topic's evidence: its `r tx$n_words` most distinctive (FREX) and most probable words and its `r tx$n_examples` most typical paragraphs. It drafts a label, a one-sentence description, and a proposition a speaker could take a side on. The file is written once: if `topic_codebook.csv` exists it is read, not redrafted, so your edits survive. Delete it to redraft.

```{r codebook}
#| results: asis
cb_path <- p_out("topic_codebook.csv")
check_inputs(cb_path, theta_out)
if (file.exists(cb_path)) {
  codebook <- readr::read_csv(cb_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  writeLines(glue::glue("Existing codebook read ({nrow(codebook)} topics); no calls made."))
} else {
  examples <- paragraph_theta |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(paragraphs, para_uid, text), by = "para_uid") |>
    dplyr::group_by(topic) |>
    dplyr::slice_max(theta_max, n = tx$n_examples, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::summarise(ex = str_c("- ", str_trunc(text, 400), collapse = "\n"))
  ev <- dplyr::left_join(topic_summary, examples, by = "topic")
  sys <- build_prompt(
    role = "You are a survey methodologist who names statistical topics so colleagues can use them.",
    task = str_c("Read one topic's words and example paragraphs from speeches in the general ",
                 "debate of the UN General Assembly. Write a short label, one factual sentence ",
                 "on what the paragraphs discuss, and one proposition: a single claim, in one ",
                 "sentence, that a paragraph on this topic could agree or disagree with. Check ",
                 "every word against the evidence."),
    rules = c("Use only the words and paragraphs shown.",
              "Do not infer which country is speaking or its intent.",
              "Do not invent statistics, dates, places, or names.",
              "The proposition states one side only: never 'X over Y' or 'X rather than Y'.",
              "If the evidence is mixed, say so plainly."),
    output = "A label of at most 4 words, a one-sentence description, and a one-sentence proposition.")
  type <- ellmer::type_object(
    label = ellmer::type_string("At most 4 words."),
    description = ellmer::type_string("One factual sentence."),
    proposition = ellmer::type_string("One claim, one sentence."))
  prompts <- str_c("Distinctive words: ", ev$frex, "\nMost probable words: ", ev$prob,
                   "\nExample paragraphs:\n", ev$ex)
  drafts <- ask_many(make_chat("codebook", sys, tx$steps, tx$use_openrouter),
                     prompts, type)
  codebook <- tibble(topic = ev$topic, label = drafts$label,
                     description = drafts$description,
                     proposition = drafts$proposition) |>
    dplyr::arrange(topic)
  readr::write_csv(codebook, cb_path, na = "")
  record_inputs(cb_path, theta_out)
  if (anyNA(codebook$label))
    warning(sum(is.na(codebook$label)), " topics got no label; name them by hand.")
}
dup <- codebook |> dplyr::add_count(label) |> dplyr::filter(n > 1, !is.na(label))
if (nrow(dup)) writeLines(glue::glue("**Duplicate labels to fix:** \\
  {str_c('topic ', dup$topic, ' (', dup$label, ')', collapse = ', ')}."))

topic_summary |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(codebook, topic, label), by = "topic") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(prevalence)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(topic, label, prevalence, paragraphs = n_paras, avepp) |>
  tbl_paged(caption = "Topics by the share of text they take up, most first.")
```

```{r codebook-records}
#| results: asis
codebook |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(topic_summary, topic, frex, prevalence), by = "topic") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(prevalence)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(title = str_c("Topic ", topic, ": ", label)) |>
  tbl_records("title", c("description", "proposition", "frex"),
              caption = "Topic codebook. Edit the CSV; nothing redrafts it.")
```

# Attention over time

For each topic, its share of each paragraph is regressed on the year spline with a fractional logit (Papke and Wooldridge 1996), so every estimated share stays between 0 and 1. The model is refit on `r tx$n_draws` draws of the topic shares and the results combined, so the 95 percent intervals include the topic model's own uncertainty and the clustering of paragraphs within a speech. The set of countries speaking changes slightly from year to year, so a trend mixes change in what speakers say with change in who spoke.

```{r effects}
draws <- withr::with_seed(tx$seed, purrr::map(seq_len(tx$n_draws), function(i)
  do.call(rbind, stm::thetaPosterior(stm_fit, nsims = 1, type = "Global"))))
grid <- sort(unique(meta$Year))
topic_trends <- purrr::map(seq_len(K), function(k)
  topic_trend(draws, k, bs, grid, meta$id)) |>
  purrr::list_rbind()
rm(draws)
arrow::write_parquet(dplyr::mutate(topic_trends, dplyr::across(c(fit, lo, hi), function(x) round(x, 5))),
                     p_out("topic_trends.parquet"))
labelled <- topic_trends |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(codebook, topic, label), by = "topic") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(topic_summary, topic, prevalence), by = "topic") |>
  dplyr::mutate(name = str_c(topic, ". ", str_trunc(label, 24)))
```

```{r heat}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Estimated share of attention by year, one row per topic, most prevalent at the top. Read it for timing: when a topic rose, peaked, and faded."
labelled |>
  dplyr::mutate(name = forcats::fct_reorder(name, prevalence)) |>
  ggplot(aes(Year, name, fill = fit)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "share", labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

```{r change}
#| results: asis
first_y <- min(grid); last_y <- max(grid)
change <- labelled |>
  dplyr::group_by(topic, label) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    start = mean(fit[Year <= first_y + 2]),
    end = mean(fit[Year >= last_y - 2]),
    peak_year = Year[which.max(fit)],
    last = fit[Year == last_y],
    before_last = mean(fit[Year >= last_y - 5 & Year < last_y]),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(change = end - start, last_vs_before = last - before_last)
change |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(change)) |>
  dplyr::slice(c(1:5, (dplyr::n() - 4):dplyr::n())) |>
  dplyr::transmute(topic, label,
                   !!glue::glue("{first_y}-{first_y + 2}") := scales::percent(start, 0.1),
                   !!glue::glue("{last_y - 2}-{last_y}") := scales::percent(end, 0.1),
                   `change (points)` = round(100 * change, 1), `peak year` = peak_year) |>
  tbl_paged(caption = glue::glue("The five topics that gained the most attention between the first and last three years, then the five that lost the most. Estimated shares from the trend model."))
change |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(abs(last_vs_before))) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 8) |>
  dplyr::transmute(topic, label,
                   !!as.character(last_y) := scales::percent(last, 0.1),
                   !!glue::glue("{last_y - 5}-{last_y - 1} average") := scales::percent(before_last, 0.1),
                   `difference (points)` = round(100 * last_vs_before, 1)) |>
  tbl_paged(caption = glue::glue("{last_y} against the five years before it: the eight topics that differ most. {last_y} is the last year on the curve, where the trend leans on earlier years; read these alongside the plots."))
```

```{r trend-plots}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Estimated share of attention by year with 95 percent intervals, nine topics per page, most prevalent first. Each panel has its own scale."
pages <- labelled |>
  dplyr::mutate(page = (dplyr::dense_rank(dplyr::desc(prevalence)) - 1) %/% 9) |>
  dplyr::group_split(page)
purrr::walk(pages, function(d) print(
  ggplot(d, aes(Year, fit)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, fill = viridis(1, begin = 0.35)) +
    geom_line(color = viridis(1, begin = 0.35)) +
    facet_wrap(~ forcats::fct_reorder(name, -prevalence), scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "estimated share")))
```

# How to read these numbers

- **Topics are found, not chosen.** The model groups words that appear together; the labels are drafted by a language model from each topic's words and paragraphs and checked by hand. A topic with low AvePP mixes subjects; read its paragraphs before relying on its trend.
- **Shares are shares of paragraphs.** A long speech contributes more than a short one, and a country that speaks every year more than one that does not.
- **Trends are smoothed.** The curve leans on neighboring years, most of all at 2000 and at `r max(grid)`, the first and last years.
- **Transcripts may contain errors.** Speeches are auto-generated transcripts; misheard words become noise in the topics.
- **Composition.** Who speaks changes slightly from year to year, so a trend mixes change in what is said with change in who said it.
